mainTopic: Whether a later act like cutting counts as 'making' a מצוה object (ציצית, סוכה, לולב), binding the לולב, and the source for valid סכך
overview: The amud opens by finishing שמואל's point: ציצית may be threaded through two corners at once. רב holds that ציצית tied while their strands were still joined become כשר once the strands are cut apart, because 'cutting is making.' שמואל, לוי, and רב מתנה say such ציצית are פסול forever. A ברייתא about ציצית, together with the rule of תעשה ולא מן העשוי from סוכה, is raised against רב. רב answers the סוכה case, but the ציצית ברייתא stays a קשיא for him. The גמרא then asks whether a תנאים dispute about picking extra berries off a הדס on יום טוב matches רב and שמואל. It rejects that comparison in two ways: perhaps the argument is whether we learn לולב from סוכה, or whether a לולב needs אגד at all. Along the way it explains that binding the לולב is a הידור מצוה based on 'זה אלי ואנוהו.' Finally, the גמרא looks for the Torah source of the rules for סכך: ריש לקיש learns them from the mist (אד), and רבי יוחנן learns them from the חגיגה offering, a source that works even for רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Why שמואל needed to teach that threading through two corners is fine
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes שמואל's teaching. One might think each string must belong to a single corner at the moment of threading. שמואל teaches that this is not required.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: we need a single corner at the moment the string is threaded, and here there isn't one. So שמואל teaches us that this is not a problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation of what is new in שמואל's ruling. One could have thought threading into two corners at once is invalid, and שמואל tells us it is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that at the moment of threading, the string runs between two corners, so it does not clearly belong to one corner. שמואל rules that what matters is the tying, not the threading. So this is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: We require
A corner of the garment
The thread or string (here: the moment of threading it)
He teaches us (the new point of the ruling)

phrases.english: we require a single corner at the time of threading the string —
phrases.notes: This is the 'you might have thought' reasoning that שמואל comes to reject.

phrases.english: and there is none here; so he teaches us (that it is fine).
phrases.notes: Here the strings were threaded into two corners at once.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵינַן כָּנָף בִּשְׁעַת פְּתִיל וְלֵיכָּא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a discussion that began on the previous amud (the novelty of שמואל's ruling).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point does שמואל's ruling teach?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One might have required a single corner at the moment of threading. שמואל teaches that this is not needed.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to refute רב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that ציצית attached without cutting the ends of the strands are פסול. If that means 'forever,' it contradicts רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'If one attached them and did not cut the ends of their strands, they are invalid.' Doesn't this mean invalid forever? Then it is a refutation of רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack רב. רב holds that ציצית attached with joined strands become כשר once they are cut apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא calls joined, uncut strands פסול. If 'פסול' means the problem can never be fixed, then cutting them later would not help. That is exactly what רב permits, so the ברייתא would disprove him.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (from a ברייתא)
He attached them (the ציצית strings)
The ends of the strands
A refutation

phrases.english: They challenged: If one attached them and did not cut
the ends of their strands — they are invalid.
phrases.notes: The strands were still joined to each other.

phrases.english: Does it not mean: invalid forever,
phrases.notes: Meaning cutting afterwards cannot fix them.

phrases.english: and this is a refutation of רב?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to רב's view about ציצית attached while joined and cut later.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that ציצית attached with joined strands and cut afterwards are כשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא means 'פסול forever,' then cutting later cannot help. That contradicts רב.

steps.title: רב reads the ברייתא as invalid only until cut
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that 'פסול' in the ברייתא means 'פסול until the strands are cut.' It does not mean forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב could say to you: What does 'invalid' mean? Invalid until they are cut.
steps.whatsHappening: רב defends himself by reading the word 'פסולין' in the ברייתא more narrowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, the ברייתא only describes the current state: while the strands are still joined, the ציצית do not work. Once they are cut apart, they become כשר. So the ברייתא and רב agree.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (a defense on someone's behalf)
Until they are cut

phrases.english: Rav could say to you: what does 'invalid' mean —
invalid until they are cut.
phrases.notes: This is a temporary invalidity that can be fixed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the ברייתא ('פסולין' means temporarily invalid)
steps.terutzMaskana: 'פסולין' means invalid only until the strands are cut.

steps.title: שמואל, לוי, and רב מתנה say invalid forever
steps.stepSummary: שמואל holds the opposite: the ציצית are פסול forever. לוי says the same, and רב מתנה reports the same in שמואל's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: invalid forever. And לוי likewise said: invalid forever. And רב מתנה likewise said in the name of שמואל: invalid forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא records the other side of the dispute. שמואל, supported by לוי and רב מתנה, reads the ברייתא as 'פסול forever.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: For these אמוראים, the strands were never properly made as separate ציצית strings. Cutting them later cannot fix this. Three voices now stand against רב's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Forever, permanently
And likewise said (a supporting opinion)

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: they are invalid forever.
And likewise Levi said: they are invalid forever.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: And likewise Rav Mattana said in the name of Shmuel:
they are invalid forever.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing reading of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ציצית attached while the strands were joined are פסול forever, and cutting later does not help.

steps.title: רב מתנה's real-life case before שמואל
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רב מתנה tells of a case that happened to him. He asked שמואל, who ruled the ציצית were פסול forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב מתנה said, 'There was an incident with me. I came before Master שמואל, and he told me: invalid forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of how רב מתנה's report reached us. It was an actual practical ruling (מעשה), not just a teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling stays the same, 'פסול forever.' The new point is the setting: שמואל gave this ruling in a real case. A ruling given in practice carries extra weight.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (an alternative version)
An incident, a real case
With me, to me

phrases.english: Some say: Rav Mattana said:
there was an incident with me,
and I came before Master Shmuel,
and he said to me: they are invalid forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה בְּדִידִי הֲוָה עוֹבָדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of רב מתנה's report from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a practical case, שמואל ruled that the ציצית are פסול forever.
steps.whatToRemember: רב: joined strands are פסול only until cut, and then כשר. שמואל, לוי, and רב מתנה: פסול forever.

steps.title: A ברייתא directly says attached then cut is invalid
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says outright that if one attached the strands and only afterwards cut them, they are פסול. This contradicts רב head-on.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'If one attached them, and afterwards cut the ends of their strands, they are invalid.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger challenge against רב. This ברייתא describes exactly רב's case and still calls it פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב escaped the first ברייתא by reading 'פסול' as 'until cut.' That answer cannot work here, because this ברייתא already includes the cutting. Even after the cutting it says פסול, which seems to refute רב directly.

keyTerms.meaning: And afterwards
He cut

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ברייתות. The first said 'did NOT cut,' which רב could explain. This one says 'cut AFTERWARDS,' which is exactly רב's own case.

phrases.english: They challenged: If one attached them, and afterwards
cut the ends of their strands, they are invalid.
phrases.notes: This is the very case where רב says כשר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי תְּלָאָן וְאַחַר כָּךְ פָּסַק רָאשֵׁי חוּטִין שֶׁלָּהֶן פְּסוּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Renews the attack on רב in a way that his answer in step 3 cannot handle.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that attaching and then cutting is כשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly includes the later cutting and still rules פסול.

steps.title: Support from סוכה: make it, not from what is already made
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a parallel ברייתא about סוכה, built on the rule 'תעשה ולא מן העשוי.' A סוכה roofed over vines still attached to the ground is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, it was taught about סוכה: 'You shall make' — and not from what is already made. From here they said: if one trained a grapevine, a gourd, or ivy over the סוכה and then put roofing on top of them, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens the challenge against רב with a parallel rule from סוכה. The ברייתא is quoted in full here, and the next step works out which case it describes in order to turn it against רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'תעשה ולא מן העשוי' means the מצוה object must be actively made in a valid way. It cannot become valid on its own when a problem is later removed. Applied to ציצית, which also uses the word 'תעשה,' strands attached in an invalid way would not become כשר just by being cut later.

keyTerms.meaning: Make it, and not from what is already made
He trained or trellised (a plant over something)
He put on roofing (סכך)
And furthermore it was taught (an additional source)

steps.whyThisMatters: This links ציצית and סוכה under one principle, 'תעשה ולא מן העשוי.' That principle is central to the whole sugya.

phrases.english: And furthermore, it was taught regarding a sukka:
'You shall make' — and not from what is already made.
phrases.notes: Learned from the פסוק about the festival of סוכות (Deuteronomy 16:13).

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ: הִדְלָה עָלֶיהָ אֶת הַגֶּפֶן
phrases.english: From here they said: if one trained a grapevine over it,
or a gourd plant, or ivy,
phrases.notes: These plants are still attached to the ground.

phrases.english: and he put roofing on top of them — it is invalid.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא ends here. The next step asks what case it describes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source that strengthens the challenge in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That something attached or made invalidly does not become כשר just because the problem is removed later. This works against רב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about סוכה: 'תעשה ולא מן העשוי' and the case of roofing over attached vines.

steps.title: Working out the case of the vine-covered סוכה, which seems to refute רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the סוכה ברייתא describes. It cannot mean vines that were never cut, since attached vines are פסול anyway. So it must mean vines that were cut, and they are still פסול. That means cutting does not count as 'making' them, and this is a refutation of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case is this? If the vines were never cut, why give the reason 'תעשה ולא מן העשוי'? They are פסול simply because they are still attached to the ground! So the case must be where he cut them, and the ברייתא still says the סוכה is פסול. Learn from this that we do not say 'cutting them is making them.' This is a refutation of רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the סוכה ברייתא from the last step and shows that it only makes sense if the vines were cut. Once we read it that way, it seems to prove רב wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the vines were never cut, the ברייתא would not need the special rule of תעשה ולא מן העשוי, because attached vines are פסול anyway. So the ברייתא must be talking about vines that were cut after roofing. Even so, the סוכה stays פסול, which shows that cutting does not turn into 'making.' That is exactly what רב claimed it does.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What case is this?
If you say (introduces a reading that will be rejected)
Let him derive it (from a simpler reason)
Their cutting is their making (רב's principle)
A strong refutation

steps.confusionAlert: The proof comes from the reason the ברייתא gives, not just from its ruling. Because it bothers to say תעשה ולא מן העשוי, it must be talking about cut vines.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say it is where he did not cut them,
why specifically because of 'You shall make'
and not from what is already made?
Derive it from the fact that they are attached to the ground!
Rather, it is where he cut them, and it teaches that it is unfit,
so learn from it that we do not say
'their cutting is their making,'
and this is a refutation of רב!
phrases.notes: A תיובתא is the strongest kind of challenge: it claims a source has disproved רב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the סוכה ברייתא brought in step 7 to turn it into a challenge against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's principle that cutting counts as making (קציצתן זו היא עשייתן).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's reason only makes sense for cut vines, and cut vines are still פסול. So cutting does not count as making.

steps.title: רב answers that the vines were yanked off, not cut
steps.stepSummary: רב can say that the סוכה ברייתא is about vines that were pulled or yanked off. That kind of removal is not a noticeable act of making, so it does not help. Real cutting still could.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can tell you: what case are we dealing with here? Where he yanked them off by pulling. In that case, their 'making' is not noticeable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב defends himself by reading the סוכה ברייתא as a special case. It is about vines that were pulled off, not cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב agrees that the vines in the ברייתא are no longer attached. He argues that pulling them off is not a clear, visible act of making. Only a real, noticeable cut counts as 'making,' so the ברייתא does not refute his principle.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (narrows a source to a specific case)
He yanked them off by pulling
Noticeable, recognizable

phrases.english: Rav could say to you:
What case are we dealing with here?
Where he pulled them off by yanking,
so their 'making' is not noticeable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation of step 8 by narrowing the ברייתא's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about vines that were properly cut, so cutting does not count as making.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about vines that were yanked off. Since that 'making' is not noticeable, it says nothing against a real cut.

steps.title: The ציצית ברייתא remains a difficulty for רב
steps.stepSummary: Even if רב escapes the סוכה ברייתא, the ציצית ברייתא, which says that attaching first and cutting afterward is פסול, still challenges him. The גמרא admits: it is indeed difficult.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the teaching 'he attached them and afterward cut them' is a difficulty for רב! It is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ציצית ברייתא from step 6, which רב has not answered. It concludes that this ברייתא stays a real difficulty for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'yanking' answer works only for the סוכה case. The ציצית ברייתא clearly speaks of cutting, which is a noticeable act, and it still says פסול. The גמרא has no answer, so it ends with 'קשיא.' That means the point is left unresolved, but it is not a full refutation.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, regardless
It is difficult (the question stands with no answer)

steps.whatToRemember: רב's view (cutting counts as making) survives the סוכה ברייתא by the 'yanking' answer. It stays difficult because of the ציצית ברייתא.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' at the end is weaker than 'תיובתא.' It means there is an unanswered difficulty, not that רב's view is completely thrown out.

phrases.aramaic: מִכׇּל מָקוֹם, תְּלָאָן וְאַחַר כָּךְ פָּסַק,
phrases.english: In any case, 'he attached them and afterward cut them'
is a difficulty for Rav!
It is a difficulty.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכׇּל מָקוֹם, תְּלָאָן וְאַחַר כָּךְ פָּסַק, קַשְׁיָא לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 9 answers the סוכה ברייתא, this step goes back to the unanswered ציצית ברייתא and closes that line of challenge.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ציצית ברייתא stays an unresolved difficulty against רב's principle.

steps.title: Suggesting a parallel dispute between תנאים about picking berries off a הדס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the רב–שמואל argument matches a dispute between תנאים. The case is a הדס whose extra berries were picked on יום טוב, which is not allowed. רבי שמעון בר יהוצדק says it is פסול, and the חכמים say it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is like a dispute between תנאים. If he did wrong and picked them off, it is פסול, says רבי שמעון בר יהוצדק. And the חכמים say it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new idea. Maybe the question of whether a later fix counts as 'making' is already argued about by תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a הדס with more black berries than leaves, which makes it פסול. Picking off berries fixes it, but doing so on יום טוב is forbidden. The question is whether this late fix, done after the item already existed, makes it כשר, much like cutting the ציצית after attaching them.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it is like a dispute between תנאים
He did wrong and picked them off
Declare it fit (כשר)
Myrtle branch, one of the ארבעה מינים

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute of tannaim.
If he transgressed and picked them, it is unfit,
phrases.notes: Refers to picking berries off a הדס on יום טוב.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yehotzadak.
And the Sages declare it fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב is left with a difficulty, the גמרא looks for a תנאים dispute that may match the רב–שמואל argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: About a הדס whose berries were picked on יום טוב: רבי שמעון בר יהוצדק says פסול, and the חכמים say כשר.

steps.title: The assumptions behind the comparison: לולב needs binding, and it learns from סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what it first assumed in order to make the comparison work. Everyone holds that a לולב needs binding (אגד) from the Torah. Everyone also learns לולב from סוכה, where 'תעשה ולא מן העשוי' applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: They thought that everyone agrees a לולב needs binding, and that we learn לולב from סוכה. As it is written about סוכה: 'You shall make,' and not from what is already made.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up how the הדס dispute connects to our question. Here it states the shared starting assumptions, and the next move will show how each side's view follows from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bound bundle must be 'made' in a valid way like a סוכה, then a הדס that became כשר only after it was bound raises the same issue: does a later fix count as 'making'? Under these assumptions, רבי שמעון בר יהוצדק would match one side and the חכמים the other. The גמרא has not yet spelled out which side matches which.

keyTerms.meaning: They assumed at first (an assumption that may later be rejected)
Binding of the לולב bundle
We learn (one law from another)
The palm branch, or the whole bundle of species

steps.confusionAlert: 'סברוה' signals only a first assumption. Be ready for the גמרא to question these assumptions later.

phrases.english: They assumed that everyone agrees
a lulav requires binding,
and we learn lulav from sukka.
As it is written regarding sukka:
'You shall make,' and not from what is already made.

steps.triggerLanguage: סַבְרוּהָ דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לוּלָב צָרִיךְ אֶגֶד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the basis for comparing the הדס dispute in step 11 to the question of 'cutting is making.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The working assumption is that everyone holds לולב needs אגד from the Torah and that לולב learns from סוכה's rule of תעשה ולא מן העשוי.

steps.title: Suggesting the תנאים argue exactly like רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the one who says כשר holds 'cutting is its making' for סוכה, so picking the berries counts as making for לולב. The one who says פסול holds the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this what they argue about? The one who says כשר holds that for סוכה we say 'their cutting is their making,' so for לולב too we say 'their picking is their making.' The one who says פסול holds that for סוכה we do not say 'their cutting is their making,' so for לולב too we do not say 'their picking is their making'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out the comparison it set up. It tries to show that the תנאים argue about the very same idea as רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדס was already tied into the bundle while it still had too many berries. Picking the berries afterward is like cutting the סכך after it was put up. If cutting counts as 'making' (like רב), picking counts too, so the הדס is כשר; if not (like שמואל), it is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? (a proposed explanation)
Their cutting is their making
Their picking (of the extra berries)
The one who rules it valid

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'making' (עשייה) is not just about fixing the הדס. The question is whether that picking, done after the bundle was already tied, can itself count as the act that makes the bundle. That is why it matters that the bundle was already tied before the picking.

phrases.english: Is it not that they argue about this:
that the one who rules it valid holds:
we say regarding סוכה,
'their cutting is their making,'
and regarding לולב too we say,
'their picking is their making.'
And the one who rules it invalid holds:
we do not say regarding סוכה,
'their cutting is their making,'
and regarding לולב too we do not say,
'their picking is their making'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the comparison set up in Step 12 by mapping each תנא onto רב or שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: That the רב–שמואל dispute is already a dispute among תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute between רבי שמעון בר יהוצדק and the חכמים about a הדס picked on יום טוב

steps.title: Rejection: the argument is only whether we learn לולב from סוכה
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that for סוכה cutting is not making. The תנאים argue only about whether the rules of לולב are learned from סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that for סוכה we do not say 'their cutting is their making.' Here they argue about learning לולב from סוכה. The one who says כשר holds we do not learn לולב from סוכה. The one who says פסול holds we do learn לולב from סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the comparison. The תנאים do not have to be arguing about the רב–שמואל question at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes the second assumption from Step 12, that everyone learns לולב from סוכה. Now the כשר view simply holds that 'תעשה ולא מן העשוי' does not apply to לולב. So it does not matter when the berries were picked.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
To learn or derive (one law from another)
We derive

phrases.english: No, for everyone agrees
we do not say regarding סוכה,
'their cutting is their making,'
and here they argue about learning לולב from סוכה.
The one who rules it valid holds:
we do not learn לולב from סוכה,
and the one who rules it invalid holds:
we do learn לולב from סוכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 13 by moving the point of argument from 'cutting is making' to whether we learn לולב from סוכה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the תנאים must be arguing about the רב–שמואל question
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that everyone learns לולב from סוכה. That assumption is not needed.

steps.title: Another rejection: the argument is whether a לולב needs binding
steps.stepSummary: If a לולב needs אגד, everyone learns it from סוכה. The תנאים actually argue about whether a לולב needs אגד at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: if we hold that a לולב needs binding, everyone agrees we learn לולב from סוכה. Here they argue about this: one master holds it needs binding, and the other holds it does not need binding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different way to push back on the comparison. This time it removes the other assumption from Step 12, that everyone requires אגד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is no required binding, the bundle is not a 'made' item, so 'תעשה ולא מן העשוי' has nothing to apply to. The one who says פסול requires אגד, so the bundle was made while still invalid. The one who says כשר does not require אגד, so it makes no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (an alternative answer)
Binding of the לולב with the other species
One master holds... and the other master holds

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: אִי סְבִירָא לַן דְּלוּלָב צָרִיךְ אֶגֶד,
phrases.english: if we hold that a לולב needs binding,
everyone does not argue
that we learn לולב from סוכה.
And here they argue about this:
one master holds: it needs binding,
and the other master holds: it does not need binding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second rejection of Step 13, separate from Step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the תנאים must be arguing about the רב–שמואל question
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that everyone requires אגד. The argument could be about that very point.

steps.title: Linking the binding argument to a known ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The argument about אגד matches a ברייתא. The תנא קמא says a לולב is כשר either way, and רבי יהודה says it is כשר only if bound.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the dispute of these תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: a לולב, whether bound or not bound, is כשר. רבי יהודה says: if bound, it is כשר; if not bound, it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the second rejection is not made up. It points to a real dispute among תנאים about whether a לולב needs binding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives a source for both sides of the אגד question. רבי שמעון בר יהוצדק matches רבי יהודה, and the חכמים match the תנא קמא of this ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute
As a ברייתא teaches
Bound together

phrases.english: And it is the dispute of these תנאים,
as it is taught: a לולב,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין אָגוּד בֵּין שֶׁאֵינוֹ אָגוּד — כָּשֵׁר,
phrases.english: whether bound or not bound, is valid.
רבי יהודה says:
bound, it is valid;
not bound, it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 15 by giving a source for the אגד dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says a לולב is כשר bound or unbound. רבי יהודה says it is כשר only if bound.

steps.title: Asking for רבי יהודה's source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה requires the לולב to be bound.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי יהודה gets the rule that binding is needed. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the ארבעה מינים never mentions binding. So the גמרא wants to know what Torah source makes it a requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: What is his reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי יהודה's view, quoted in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for requiring אגד

steps.title: רבי יהודה learns binding from the bundle of hyssop
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה uses a גזירה שוה on the word 'taking.' Just as the אזוב in Egypt was taken as a bundle, the ארבעה מינים must be taken as a bundle.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns 'taking' from 'taking' in the bundle of hyssop. There it is written: 'Take a bundle of hyssop.' Here it is written: 'And you shall take for yourselves on the first day.' Just as there it was in a bundle, so too here it must be in a bundle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a גזירה שוה. The same word 'ולקחתם' appears in two places, so a rule from one place carries over to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the קרבן פסח in מצרים clearly says the אזוב was a bundle (אגודה). Because the same word 'taking' is used for the ארבעה מינים, רבי יהודה applies the bundle rule to them too.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking (the shared word of the גזירה שוה)
Bundle of hyssop (used in מצרים for the blood of the פסח)
Just as there... so too here

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה requires אגד from the Torah, through a גזירה שוה of 'לקיחה' from אגודת אזוב.

phrases.english: He learns 'taking' from 'taking'
from the bundle of hyssop.
It is written there: 'Take a bundle of hyssop,'
and it is written here:
'And you shall take for yourselves on the first day.'
Just as there it is in a bundle,
so too here it is in a bundle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of 'לקיחה' from אגודת אזוב

steps.title: The רבנן reject the גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן do not learn 'taking' from 'taking,' so they do not require binding.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן hold: we do not learn 'taking' from 'taking.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן disagree. They do not accept this גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the גזירה שוה, nothing in the Torah requires binding. So for the רבנן a לולב is כשר even if it is not bound. In our case, this means picking the הדס's berries after it was bound does not make it פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (here, the majority view in the ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: According to this second approach, the הדס dispute depends on אגד. Whoever requires binding says פסול, and whoever does not require it says כשר. This does not prove anything about רב and שמואל.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis: we do not learn 'taking' from 'taking.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side's reasoning, which completes the explanation of the אגד dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן do not accept the גזירה שוה, so they do not require אגד.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the ברייתא about binding the לולב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which opinion matches a ברייתא that says binding the לולב is a מצוה, yet an unbound לולב is still כשר. Neither רבי יהודה nor the רבנן seems to fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion does this ברייתא follow: 'It is a מצוה to bind the לולב, but if he did not bind it, it is still כשר'? If it is רבי יהודה, why is it כשר when unbound? If it is the רבנן, why is binding a מצוה at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a 'middle' position on binding and asks which side of the argument it belongs to. It shows that each option has a problem, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says binding is required, so an unbound לולב should be פסול, but the ברייתא says it is כשר. The רבנן say binding is not needed at all, so it is strange for the ברייתא to call it a מצוה. The ברייתא seems to fit neither view.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion does it follow?
To bind it (the לולב with the הדסים and ערבות)
If it is this one... if it is that one... (a two-sided dilemma)
Why?

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is that which is taught in a baraita:
A lulav, it is a מצוה to bind it,
and if he did not bind it, it is fit.
If it is Rabbi Yehuda,
when he did not bind it, why is it fit?
If it is the Rabbis, why is it a מצוה?
phrases.notes: The רבנן do not require binding at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the רבי יהודה / רבנן argument from steps 16-19 against a ברייתא that seems to take a middle position.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that binding is a מצוה but does not affect whether the לולב is כשר?

steps.title: It is the רבנן, because a מצוה should be done beautifully
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows the רבנן. Binding is not required, but it is a מצוה because of הידור מצוה, which comes from the פסוק 'זה אלי ואנוהו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is the רבנן. It is a מצוה only because the Torah says 'This is my God and I will beautify Him.' This means: make yourself beautiful before Him in doing מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows the רבנן. Binding is not needed for the לולב to be כשר, but it is a nicer way to do the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'מצוה' in the ברייתא is not a basic requirement of the מצוה of לולב. It is a separate value of beautifying מצוות. So the רבנן can say an unbound לולב is כשר and still say binding is a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (keeping the original option)
'This is my God and I will beautify Him' (שמות טו:ב)
Beautify yourself before Him in doing מצוות (הידור מצוה)

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, binding the לולב is not required for it to be כשר. It is a מצוה only as הידור, based on 'זה אלי ואנוהו'.
steps.confusionAlert: Here the word 'מצוה' does not mean 'required.' It means a beautiful extra way of doing the מצוה. Without it, the מצוה is still done properly.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for הידור מצוה. The binding of the לולב that is done in practice rests on this idea.

phrases.english: Actually, it is the Rabbis,
and it is a מצוה because it is stated: 'This is my God and I will glorify Him,'
meaning: beautify yourself before Him in מצוות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma by placing the ברייתא with the רבנן and explaining that the 'מצוה' is הידור.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows the רבנן. Binding is a מצוה of beautification (זה אלי ואנוהו), not a requirement for the לולב to be כשר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An unbound לולב is כשר, but binding it is a הידור מצוה.

steps.title: What is the source for the rule about valid roofing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's general rule: סכך must not be something that is מקבל טומאה, and it must grow from the ground. It then asks where this rule comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'This is the rule: anything that can become טמא, and so on.' Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and starts a new topic. It asks for the Torah source of the rule about what may be used as סכך, which sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives two conditions for סכך: it must not be מקבל טומאה, and גידולו מן הארץ (it grew from the ground). The גמרא wants a פסוק that teaches both conditions together.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
Able to become ritually impure
From where do we know these things?

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁמְּקַבֵּל טוּמְאָה כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: This is the principle: anything that is susceptible to ritual impurity, etc.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of לולב and goes back to the next clause of the משנה about סכך.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for requiring סכך that is not מקבל טומאה and grows from the ground.

steps.title: ריש לקיש learns it from the mist rising from the earth
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns the rule from 'ואד יעלה מן הארץ.' Mist is not מקבל טומאה and rises from the ground, so סכך must be the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: the פסוק says 'And a mist went up from the earth.' Just as mist cannot become טמא and comes from the ground, so too סוכה roofing must be something that cannot become טמא and grows from the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives the first answer. He compares the סוכה to a cloud, the mist that rose from the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the סוכה recalls the clouds that surrounded בני ישראל in the desert. So סכך should be like a cloud. Mist is not מקבל טומאה and comes up from the ground, which gives both conditions of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא of ארץ ישראל (רבי שמעון בן לקיש)
The פסוק says
Mist or cloud (בראשית ב:ו)
It grows (or comes) from the ground

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: the verse states:
'And a mist went up from the earth.'

phrases.aramaic: מָה אֵד — דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל טוּמְאָה
phrases.english: Just as mist is a thing that is not susceptible to impurity
and its growth is from the ground,

phrases.aramaic: אַף סוּכָּה — דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין מְקַבֵּל טוּמְאָה
phrases.english: so too a sukka must be a thing not susceptible to impurity
and whose growth is from the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first source for the rule asked about in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סכך is compared to the mist (אד): not מקבל טומאה, and it comes from the ground.

steps.title: This works only if the desert סוכות were clouds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש. Comparing סכך to a cloud only makes sense if the סוכות in the desert were ענני כבוד. If they were real huts, there is no reason to compare סכך to a cloud.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says the סוכות were ענני כבוד. But for the one who says they made real huts for themselves, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's source. His comparison depends on one side of an argument about what the desert סוכות were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison between סוכה and cloud only holds if the סוכה we build today recalls the clouds. According to the view that the desert סוכות were real huts, the link to the cloud breaks, and ריש לקיש's source falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well for X, but for Y...
Clouds of Glory that surrounded בני ישראל in the desert
Actual, physical huts
What can be said? (there seems to be no answer)

phrases.aramaic: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר עַנְנֵי כָבוֹד הָיוּ.
phrases.english: This works well according to the one who said they were clouds of glory.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר סוּכּוֹת מַמָּשׁ עָשׂוּ לָהֶם,
phrases.english: But according to the one who said they made actual sukkot for themselves,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר עַנְנֵי כָבוֹד הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's derivation from step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's comparison of סכך to the mist (cloud).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The cloud comparison assumes the desert סוכות were ענני כבוד. According to the view that they were real huts, there is no basis to compare סכך to a cloud.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing the תנאים argue about the desert סוכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that רבי אליעזר holds the desert סוכות were ענני כבוד, while רבי עקיבא holds they were real huts. It then repeats the challenge against ריש לקיש according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'For I made בני ישראל dwell in סוכות.' These were ענני כבוד, says רבי אליעזר. רבי עקיבא says: they made real huts for themselves. This works for רבי אליעזר, but for רבי עקיבא, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that the argument mentioned in the last step really exists by quoting the ברייתא. It then restates the challenge using the names of the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know the two sides are רבי אליעזר (clouds) and רבי עקיבא (real huts). ריש לקיש's source works only for רבי אליעזר. So we still need a source that also works for רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
I caused to dwell (ויקרא כג:מג)
These are the words of רבי אליעזר
תנא who holds the desert סוכות were real huts

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: ״כִּי בַסּוּכּוֹת הוֹשַׁבְתִּי אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״,
phrases.english: As it is taught: 'For I made the children of Israel dwell in sukkot,'

phrases.aramaic: עַנְנֵי כָבוֹד הָיוּ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.english: these were clouds of glory; this is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: סוּכּוֹת מַמָּשׁ עָשׂוּ לָהֶם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: they made actual sukkot for themselves.
This works well according to Rabbi Eliezer,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר?
phrases.english: but according to Rabbi Akiva, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: ״כִּי בַסּוּכּוֹת הוֹשַׁבְתִּי אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Documents the dispute assumed in step 24 and restates the challenge with the named תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a real תנאים dispute over whether the desert סוכות were clouds or huts.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: רבי אליעזר (ענני כבוד) versus רבי עקיבא (סוכות ממש).

steps.title: רבי יוחנן compares סוכה to the חגיגה offering
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports a source from רבי יוחנן that works for everyone. 'חג הסוכות' links סוכה to the חגיגה offering, which is not מקבל טומאה and grows from the ground, so סכך must be the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the פסוק says 'Make for yourself the חג of סוכות.' This compares סוכה to the חגיגה offering. Just as the חגיגה is something that cannot become טמא and grows from the ground, so too the סוכה must be something that cannot become טמא and grows from the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new source that does not depend on clouds, so it works even for רבי עקיבא. The Torah's words 'חג הסוכות' tie the סוכה to the festival offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'חג' in 'חג הסוכות' creates a היקש between סוכה and the חגיגה animal. A living animal is not מקבל טומאה, and it grows by eating plants from the ground. So both conditions for סכך are learned without needing the cloud idea.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Compares, links through a היקש
The festival peace-offering brought on יום טוב
'Make for yourself the festival of סוכות' (דברים טז:יג)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources for the rules of סכך. ריש לקיש uses the mist (אד), which fits only רבי אליעזר. רבי יוחנן uses the חגיגה offering, which fits everyone, including רבי עקיבא.
steps.confusionAlert: The חגיגה here means the animal itself, not the act of offering it. A live animal grows by eating from the ground and is not מקבל טומאה, and that is why it can serve as the model for סכך.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
The verse states: 'You shall make for yourself the festival of Sukkot,'
it likens the sukka to the festival offering.

phrases.aramaic: מָה חֲגִיגָה — דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל טוּמְאָה
phrases.english: Just as the festival offering is a thing not susceptible to impurity
and its growth is from the ground,

phrases.aramaic: אַף סוּכָּה — דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל טוּמְאָה
phrases.english: so too the sukka must be a thing not susceptible to impurity
and whose growth is from the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 24-25 by giving a source that works even according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A היקש from 'חג הסוכות' compares סוכה to the חגיגה: not מקבל טומאה, and it grows from the ground.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rules for סכך are learned from the חגיגה offering, a source that works for רבי עקיבא too.
